<SUMMARY>
Global geopolitical dynamics are largely shaped by technological competition and resource security, with significant developments observed in AI infrastructure and critical mineral supply chains. SoftBank plans substantial AI data center investments in France, highlighting Europe's drive to catch up with dominant US and Chinese AI capabilities. Concurrently, the US has expanded export controls targeting Chinese-affiliated overseas subsidiaries, aiming to redesign China's AI chip industry. In the critical minerals sector, Brazil is emerging as an alternative to China for rare earth elements, while the US secured a rare earth deal in Greenland, intensifying global competition. The ongoing conflict in West Asia, particularly the Iran war, continues to disrupt global oil supply routes and has prompted regional states to focus on energy security and renewable investments, impacting both the EU's Russian oil price cap considerations and global market stability. Military actions in West Asia include an Israeli incursion into Lebanon and Iran's deployment of an IRGC ship in the Strait of Hormuz. India continues to strengthen its domestic semiconductor and military drone manufacturing sectors while facing economic challenges from the West Asia conflict.
</SUMMARY>
<EWS>
The widening crisis in West Asia, driven by the ongoing Iran war into its fourth month, poses a top-tier risk to energy security and global oil supply routes, prompting BlackRock to flag it. The EU's consideration of a temporary freeze on the Russian oil price cap signals potential instability in energy markets and geopolitical alignments. Iran's deployment of an IRGC ship in the Strait of Hormuz and plans for transit fees could further heighten regional tensions and impact maritime security. The escalating US export controls, now targeting Chinese-affiliated overseas subsidiaries, indicate increasing pressure on China's AI chip industry and global supply chains, with Huawei acknowledging the sanctions spurred its domestic R&D. The deepening Israeli incursion into Lebanon marks a significant escalation, with Israeli troops seizing a strategic castle.
</EWS>
<EXEC>
**Asia:**
China is being forced to redesign its AI chip industry due to US export curbs. Huawei's chairman stated that U.S. sanctions spurred semiconductor growth in China, encouraging R&D and building their own tech stack to compete with American technology. The Chinese AI model company MiniMax Group is preparing for a mainland China listing after shares surged in Hong Kong, aiming for a dual-listing status. WPG identified that the AI era will reward supply-chain ecosystems over individual firms. South Korea's Deputy Prime Minister and ICT Minister Bae Ky stated that South Korea should now try to build frontier artificial intelligence models on par with those of the US and China. Bitcoin’s network hash rate stalled as miners redirect power and capital toward AI data center workloads.

**Europe:**
SoftBank plans to invest 75 billion euros in France to develop and operate 5 GW of AI data center capacity, with an initial 3.1 GW of facilities planned for the country's north, leveraging France's nuclear grid. Intel targets a new AI data centre chip by year-end.

**Americas:**
Microsoft Build 2026, opening on June 2 in San Francisco, is expected to feature AI agents, GitHub Copilot updates, and Windows local AI. South Korea's Deputy Prime Minister and ICT Minister Bae Ky stated that South Korea should now try to build frontier artificial intelligence models on par with those of the US and China.
</EXEC>
<LITHO>
**Europe:**
ASML remains a wide-moat compounder, directly benefiting from semiconductor industry expansion, but its stock has been downgraded to a hold. Nikon is leveraging in-house manufacturing to reduce prices, aiming to break ASML's lithography monopoly and attract American chipmakers.
</LITHO>
<REE>
**Americas:**
Resolution Copper, a brownfield mining project in Arizona, is projected to boost America's ability to reshore its domestic copper needs. Brazil is seeing increasing demand for its vast reserves of rare earth elements, with global mining giants betting on it as the next powerhouse for critical magnetic metals and an alternative to China's dominance. The U.S. has secured a rare earth deal in Greenland.

**Africa:**
The NSCDC has arraigned 15 Chinese and nine Nigerians in Abuja for alleged illegal mining in Nasarawa. The DRC’s Congo Lithium Royalty Tax will increase to a 10% strategic rate in 2026. Zimbabwe has secured a billion dollars in value-added lithium investments from China. Africa faces new competition for critical minerals investment as the U.S. secures a Greenland rare earth deal in a bid to cut China reliance, impacting the continent's strategic mineral landscape.
</REE>
<GEO>
**Asia:**
The U.S. has expanded export controls to target Chinese-affiliated overseas subsidiaries. Huawei's chairman, in response to U.S. sanctions, thanked the US for spurring semiconductor growth, stating that Washington’s export controls encouraged Chinese firms to invest in R&D and build their own tech stack competing with American technology. U.S. export curbs are forcing China to redesign its AI chip industry.

**Americas:**
The U.S. has expanded export controls to target Chinese-affiliated overseas subsidiaries. Huawei's chairman stated that U.S. sanctions spurred semiconductor growth in China, encouraging R&D and building their own tech stack competing with American technology.

**Oceania:**
Rio Tinto Group's aluminum shipments to the US have rebounded to levels from before President Donald Trump’s tariff offensive.
</GEO>
<MILITARY>
**Asia:**
Türkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated that Türkiye is eager to cooperate with Japan in the field of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), noting potential for joint development. SpaceX set a record for flying the largest and most powerful rocket in history.

**Americas:**
SpaceX is on the verge of launching more satellites than the rest of the world combined since Sputnik. Elon Musk’s plan to launch 1 million AI data center satellites into orbit starting in 2028 is projected to spark a financial catastrophe, sending SpaceX into a high-speed nosedive.

**Oceania:**
The Pentagon chief sounded an 'alarm' over China’s military buildup and urged allies to boost defense spending.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>
The intersection of technological competition and geopolitical tensions is evident across multiple regions. SoftBank's significant AI investments in France highlight Europe's efforts to enhance its AI infrastructure, while US export controls continue to pressure China's AI chip sector, leading to China's domestic R&D acceleration. The global race for critical minerals is intensifying, with Brazil and Greenland emerging as key players, alongside Chinese investments in African lithium. The ongoing Iran war and associated military actions in West Asia underscore regional instability and its broader impact on global energy security and maritime trade.
</CONCLUSION>
<INDIA>
The Jagiroad semiconductor plant in Assam is expected to commence production this financial year, as confirmed by Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. India’s military drone manufacturing industry is projected to expand four-to-five-fold by March 2028. German chipmaker Infineon plans to expand its India operations through new R&D and supply chain investments, intending to nearly double its local workforce by 2030 to support India's green energy goals via new design partnerships and startup collaborations. Intel is investing US$3.3 billion in an India Substrate Plant. India's market capitalization reached $4.92 trillion as of May 26, slightly trailing Taiwan's $4.95 trillion. India's AI deal with the UAE challenges U.S. cloud dominance. The country faces economic challenges stemming from the West Asia war, including rising energy prices and a weaker rupee, with concerns that a poor monsoon could exacerbate food inflation and impact rural demand and growth.
</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>
The war in the Middle East continues into its fourth month. The Energy Crisis is expected to long outlast the Iran War, with BlackRock flagging energy security as a top-tier risk amid the conflict's fallout. Middle East conflict prompts renewed focus on energy security and system resilience. Dubai is implementing innovative tech-driven responses to enhance food system resilience, prompted by the Iran war. The EU is considering a temporary freeze to its price cap on Russian oil due to the war in the Middle East. US Treasury Secretary announced that Iran is ready to abandon its nuclear program. A US missile strike disabled a ship in the Gulf of Oman amid Iran tensions. Iran deployed an IRGC ship in the Strait of Hormuz and plans to implement transit fees. Israeli troops captured a strategic mountain topped with a Crusader-built castle in southern Lebanon, marking the deepest incursion into the country in over 26 years. A senior Israeli diplomat responded mockingly to France’s request for an extraordinary UNSC meeting regarding Israel’s advance into Lebanon. Cyprus is seeking assurances that a future British government will not unilaterally use its UK military bases for Middle East strikes. The Iran conflict has disrupted oil supply, leading Gulf states to explore multi-billion-dollar investments in renewables. India’s AI deal with the UAE challenges U.S. cloud dominance. Wall Street is set for record highs, with AI push eclipsing US-Iran war worries. Former Trump energy chief sounded an alarm on gas prices as the Iran conflict rattles oil markets.
</WEST_ASIA>
<FINAL_CONCLUSION>
The coming period will likely see continued intensification in the global technology and resource competition, driven by AI development and strategic mineral acquisition. US export controls are poised to further shape China's AI industry evolution, while European nations seek to bolster their own AI infrastructure. The West Asia conflict's enduring impact on global energy markets and regional security will necessitate ongoing vigilance, potentially influencing international alliances and investment flows into renewable energy. India's strategic push for self-reliance in semiconductors and military technology will be a key factor in its regional and global positioning, particularly as it navigates economic headwinds from the West Asia crisis. The re-emergence of alternative critical mineral sources in Brazil and the US deal in Greenland will likely diversify supply chains, reducing dependence on single dominant suppliers.
</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
